source_text:
εὐαγγέλιον ἀληθὲς ὂν καὶ ἀψευδές. ∆ιὰ τοῦ προσθεῖναι καθὼς καὶ ἐν παντὶ τῷ
κόσμῳ τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν βεβαιοῖ· οὐ γὰρ 317 μόνον φησὶν μέχρις ὑμῶν ἔφθασε τὸ
εὐαγγέλιον, ἀλλ' ἤδη καὶ εἰς πάντα τὸν κόσμον, ὅπερ σημεῖον τῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ
δυνάμεώς ἐστι τῆς ἐνεργούσης ἐν τῷ κηρύγματι. Οὐ γὰρ ἠμελήθη, ἀλλὰ καρποφορεῖ
καὶ αὔξεται. 316,col2 Τὴν ἐλπίδα δὲ τὴν ἀποκειμένην τῆς ἀναστάσεως καὶ τῆς
βασιλείας οὐκ ἀγγέλων διοίκησις κατώρθωσεν, ἀλλὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ παρουσία. Καὶ
τὸ εὐαγγέλιον δὲ τοῦ παρόντος εἰς ὑμᾶς, φησίν, οὐκ ἔστι ψεῦδος, ἵνα παροφθῇ· οὐδὲ
εἰς μόνους ὑμᾶς ἔφθασεν, ἀλλ' εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους. καὶ οὐκ ἔφθασε μέν,
παρηκούσθη δέ, ἀλλ' ἔστι καρποφορούμενον καὶ αὐξανόμενον. 317 Kol 1,7 Συνίστησι
τὸν Ἐπαφρᾶν ἕνα ὄντα τῶν ἁγίων καὶ κατηχήσοντα αὐτούς, ἵνα μᾶλλον αὐτοῦ τῇ
διδασκαλίᾳ προσέχωσιν. Kol 1,9 Τί δὲ ἦν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ; τὸ ἐπιγνῶναι ὑμᾶς καὶ
εἰδέναι ὅτι οὐ δι' ἀγγέλων σωθῆναι ὑμᾶς δυνατὸν ἀλλὰ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. πῶς οὖν
ἐπιγνωσόμεθα; ἐν σοφίᾳ πνευματικῇ, οὐ κοσμικῇ. Kol 1,11 Μάλιστα ἐπήγαγεν τῇ
ὑπομονῇ τὴν μακροθυμίαν· ὑπομονὴ γὰρ ἄνευ μακροθυμίας οὐχ ἵσταται καὶ ἄνευ
χαρᾶς ὑπομονὴ μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχει. δεῖ δὲ μάλιστα ἐν τούτοις καὶ χαρᾶς· οὐ γὰρ ὁ
λυπούμενος ἐπὶ ταῖς θλίψεσι ταῖς διὰ Χριστόν, ἀλλ' ὁ χαίρων ἐπ' αὐταῖς ὑποδέχεται
παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν μισθόν. τίς δὲ ὁ μισθός; ἡ υἱοθεσία, ἡ κληρονομία, ἡ μετ' ἀγγέλων
διαγωγή. Kol 1,13–14 Καὶ πρὸ τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ καὶ μετὰ τὸν κατακλυσμόν, καὶ πρὸ
τοῦ νόμου καὶ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ διηκόνουν οἱ ἄγγελοι τῷ θεῷ πρὸς τὴν ὑμετέραν
σωτηρίαν. ἀλλ' οὐκ μετέστησεν ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ νῦν διὰ
τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν, τοῦ μονογενοῦς αὐτοῦ, ἡ βασιλεία 318 αὐτοῦ ἡμῖν δεδώρηται. τὸ
δὲ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἀγάπης αὐτοῦ, οὐχ ὅτι τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ υἱός ἐστι ὁ Χριστός, ἀλλ'
ὥσπερ υἱοὶ τῆς ἀπειθείας τινὲς καὶ υἱοὶ γεέννης ἕτεροι καὶ υἱὸς ἀπωλείας ὁ διάβολος
καὶ ἄλλος υἱὸς τούτου ὠνομάσθη ᾧ προσέδραμε καὶ προσέθετο, οὐ φύσει ὢν υἱὸς
ἀλλὰ τῇ τοῦ τρόπου οἰκειότητι, οὕτω καὶ ὁ σωτὴρ υἱὸς τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ
προσηγορεύθη, ὅτι οὐ μόνον τῇ φύσει υἱὸς θεοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ τῇ τῆς ἀγάπης γνησιότητι·
ἀγαπᾶ γάρ, φησίν, τὸν υἱὸν ὁ πατήρ, καὶ πάντα δέδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ πατὴρ εἰς τὰς χεῖρας
αὐτοῦ· ἢ ὅτι ἀγαπήσας ἡμᾶς ἔπαθεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν. οὕτω δὲ ἀναγνωστέον· εἰς τὴν
βασιλείαν τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ. 317,col2 Καὶ πρὸ τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ καὶ μετὰ
κατακλυσμόν, πρὸ τοῦ νόμου καὶ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ᾖσαν ἄγγελοι ὑπηρετούμενοι τῷ θεῷ
πρὸς τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν, ἀλλ' οὐδὲν κατώρθωσαν. νυνὶ δὲ ὁ θεὸς διὰ τῆς
οἰκονομίας τοῦ κυρίου μετέστησεν ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ. ὃν ἠγάπησεν·
318,col2 ἀγγέλους μὲν γὰρ ὡς λειτουργοὺς ἀγαπᾷ, Χριστὸν δὲ ὡς υἱόν. οὐκ ἤγαγεν
οὖν ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἀλλ' εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἀγάπης αὐτοῦ.
ὑπὸ τὸν κληρονόμον ἐσμέν, οὐχ ὑπὸ τοὺς οἰκέτας. υἱὸν οὖν ἀγάπης λέγει, ἐπειδὴ ὡς
υἱὸς ἀγαπᾶται, οὐκ ἐπειδὴ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν, οὐδὲ γὰρ οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς ἀπειθείας
ταύτης υἱοὶ φύσει, οὐδὲ οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς γεέννης ταύτης τέκνα, οὐδὲ υἱὸς φύσει ἀπωλείας
ὁ διάβολος, οὐδὲ υἱὸς ἁμαρτίας ὁ ἀντικείμενος· οὕτως οὐδὲ τῆς ἀγάπης υἱὸς ὁ
κύριος. ἀλλ' ἐπειδή εἰσιν ἀγαπώμενοι δοῦλοι, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς ὡς υἱὸς ἀγαπᾶται, εἶπεν· τοῦ
υἱοῦ τῆς ἀγάπης αὐτοῦ. –Η οὕτως· μετέστησεν ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῆς ἀγάπης
τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ. ἐπειδὴ ἀγαπήσας ἡμᾶς ὁ υἱὸς ἔπαθεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, ἵνα τῆς βασιλείας
αὐτοῦ καταξιώσῃ ἡμᾶς, διὰ τοῦτό φησιν· μετέστησεν ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ
υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ· τὸ γὰρ ἀπαράλλακτον ἔχων πρὸς τὸν γεγεννηκότα κατὰ τὸ ἀγαπῆσαι καὶ
εὐεργετῆσαι τοὺς ἁμαρτωλούς, εἰκών ἐστι τοῦ πατρός. 319 Kol 1,15–17 Βούλεται
εἰπεῖν ὅτι προῆν· εἰ γὰρ μὴ προῆν πάντων, πῶς τὰ πάντα ἐν αὐτῷ κτίζεται; ἐν αὐτῷ
δὲ εἶπε κτίζεσθαι τὰ πάντα, ἵνα ἀποστάντες τοῦ ἐλπίζειν εἰς ἀγγέλους ἐλπίδα ἔχωμεν
εἰς Χριστόν· τὸ δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀντὶ τοῦ δι' αὐτοῦ. ταῦτα δὲ εἴρηται πρὸς Ἰουδαίους, ἵνα
μὴ ἐκ τότε νομίσωσιν εἶναι ἐξ οὗ γέγονεν ἐν σώματι μετ' αὐτῶν. τὰ πάντα δι' αὐτοῦ
καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν ἔκτισται. ἀντὶ τοῦ εἰς αὐτὸν ἀνατρέχει τῆς κτίσεως ἡ αἰτία· ἢ εἰς αὐτὸν
εἶπεν, ὅτι οὐδὲν τῶν κτισθέντων ἔξω αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ πάντα ὑπ' αὐτοῦ περιέχεται. καὶ
τὰ πάντα ἐν αὐτῷ συνέστηκεν· ἤτοι δι' αὐτοῦ, ἢ ἀντὶ τοῦ ἐν βουλήσει αὐτοῦ καὶ
δυνάμει διακρατεῖν τὰ πάντα κατὰ τὸ μυστήριον τὸ ἀποκεκρυμμένον ἐν τῷ θεῷ τῷ
τὰ πάντα κτίσαντι. Ἵνα σοι δείξῃ ὅτι καὶ πρὸ πάντων ἐστίν, εἴρηκεν ὅτι καὶ
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing Colossians 1:5-6] ... gospel, being true and without falsehood. By adding "as also in all the world" he confirms their faith; for not only, he says, as far as you did the gospel reach, but already into all the world, which is a sign of the power of Christ working in the preaching. For it was not neglected, but bears fruit and grows.
[Second catena form, 316 col. 2:] The hope laid up, of the resurrection and the kingdom, not the administration of angels accomplished, but the coming of Jesus Christ. And the gospel that is present to you, he says, is not a lie, so as to be overlooked; nor did it reach you alone, but all human beings. And it did not reach (you) and then go unheard, but it is bearing fruit and growing.
Colossians 1:7. He commends Epaphras as being one of the saints and as one who would instruct them, so that they may pay more heed to his teaching.
Colossians 1:9. And what was the will of God? That you recognize and know that it is not possible for you to be saved through angels but through Jesus Christ. How then shall we recognize it? In spiritual wisdom, not worldly.
Colossians 1:11. Most of all he added long-suffering to endurance; for endurance without long-suffering does not stand, and without joy endurance has no reward. And in these things there is need most of all of joy too; for not the one grieving at the afflictions for Christ's sake, but the one rejoicing at them receives the reward from God. And what is the reward? The adoption, the inheritance, the life spent with angels.
Colossians 1:13-14. Both before the flood and after the flood, and before the law and in the law, the angels were serving God for your salvation. But God did not transfer us into his kingdom; but now through our Lord, his Only-begotten, his kingdom has been given to us. And the words "of the Son of his love": not that Christ is son of the love of God, but just as some are sons of disobedience and others sons of Gehenna and the devil son of perdition, and another was named son of this to which he ran and attached himself, not being son by nature but by kinship of manner, so the Saviour too was called son of the love of God, because he is son of God not only by nature but also by the genuineness of love: for the Father loves the Son, it says, and the Father has given all things into his hands. Or because, having loved us, he suffered for us. And it should be read thus: "into the kingdom of the love of his Son."
[Second catena form, 317-318 col. 2:] Both before the flood and after the flood, before the law and in the law there were angels serving God for our salvation, but they accomplished nothing. But now God through the economy of the Lord transferred us into his kingdom. "Whom he loved": for he loves angels as ministers, but Christ as son. So he did not bring you into the (kingdom) of the angels, but into the kingdom of the Son of his love. We are under the heir, not under the household slaves. So he says "son of love" because he is loved as a son, not because he is of the love of God; for neither are the sons of this disobedience sons by nature, nor the sons of this Gehenna children, nor is the devil son of perdition by nature, nor the adversary son of sin; so neither is the Lord son of love. But since there are servants who are loved, while the Son is loved as son, he said "of the Son of his love." Or thus: he transferred us into the kingdom of the love of his Son. Since the Son, having loved us, suffered for us so that he might make us worthy of his kingdom, for this reason he says: he transferred us into the kingdom of his Son; for having exact likeness to the one who begot him in loving and doing good to sinners, he is the image of the Father.
Colossians 1:15-17. He wants to say that he existed before; for if he did not exist before all things, how are all things created in him? And he said all things are created in him, so that, standing away from hoping in angels, we may have hope in Christ; and "in him" is in place of "through him." These things were said to the Jews, so that they may not think that he exists (only) from the time when he came into being in a body with them. All things have been created through him and for (into) him. In place of: the cause of creation runs back up to him. Or he said "into him" because nothing of the created things is outside him, but all things are contained by him. "And all things hold together in him": either through him, or in place of: to hold all things fast in his will and power, according to the mystery hidden in God who created all things.
[Second form, unmarked repetition:] So that he may show you that he is also before all things, he has said that he also [continues in the next section: was begotten firstborn of all creation]
pass_b_english: … gospel, which is true and free of falsehood. By adding “as also in all the world”, he strengthens their faith. The gospel has reached not only you, he says, but already the whole world, and that is a sign of the power of Christ at work in the preaching. “For it was not neglected; it bears fruit and grows.”
On Colossians 1:7: He commends Epaphras as one of the saints and as the man who would instruct them, so that they would listen all the more to his teaching.

On Colossians 1:9: What was God’s will? That you should recognize and know that you cannot be saved through angels, only through Jesus Christ. How, then, are we to come to know it? In wisdom that is spiritual, not worldly.

On Colossians 1:11: Above all, he joined long-suffering to endurance. Endurance does not hold firm without long-suffering, and endurance without joy earns no reward. Joy, more than anything, is needed here. It is not the one who grieves over afflictions suffered for Christ who receives the reward from God, but the one who rejoices in them. And what is the reward? Adoption as sons, the inheritance, and a life spent with the angels.

On Colossians 1:13–14: Before the flood and after it, before the law and under the law, the angels served God for your salvation. Yet that is not how God brought us into his kingdom. It is now, through our Lord, his Only-begotten, that his kingdom has been given to us. As for “the Son of his love”: this does not mean that Christ is a son born of God’s love. Some people are called sons of disobedience (Ephesians 2:2), others sons of Gehenna (Matthew 23:15), and the devil a son of perdition; and anyone else is named the son of whatever he has run to and attached himself to. He is not a son by nature but by likeness of character. In the same way the Saviour was called Son of God’s love, because he is Son of God not by nature only but also by the true bond of love. “The Father loves the Son,” it says, “and has given all things into his hand” (John 3:35). Or it is because he loved us and suffered for us. And the phrase should be read like this: “into the kingdom of the love of his Son.”

The second catena form adds: … but they achieved nothing. Now God has brought us into his kingdom through the Lord’s saving dispensation. “Whom he loved”: he loves the angels as ministers, but Christ as his Son. So he did not bring you into the kingdom of the angels, but into the kingdom of the Son of his love. We are under the heir, not under the household slaves. … Nor is the adversary a son of sin by nature … Servants are loved too, but the Son is loved as a son; that is why he said “of the Son of his love”. … The Son loved us and suffered for us so that he might make us worthy of his kingdom … For since he is exactly like the one who begot him in loving sinners and doing them good, he is the image of the Father.

On Colossians 1:15–17: He means that Christ existed before. If he did not exist before all things, how are all things created in him? He said that all things are created in him so that we would stop putting our hope in angels and set our hope on Christ. “In him” stands for “through him”. This was said to the Jews, so that they would not think he existed only from the time when he came among them in a body. “All things have been created through him and for him.” This means that the cause of creation goes back to him. Or he said “for him” because nothing created is outside him; all things are held within him. “And in him all things hold together”: either “through him”, or it means that he holds all things fast by his will and power, according to the mystery hidden in God, who created all things.
The second catena form adds: To show you that he is also before all things, he has said that he was also …

choices.term: 316,col2 Τὴν ἐλπίδα δὲ … καρποφορούμενον καὶ αὐξανόμενον.
choices.english: Doublet collapsed completely (Colossians 1:5–6, second catena form)
choices.why: Every sentence of the second form has a counterpart in the first (hope not won by angels; the gospel is true and not to be overlooked; it reached all; it bears fruit and grows). Nothing added, so no 'adds' paragraph.

choices.term: 317,col2 Καὶ πρὸ τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ … εἰκών ἐστι τοῦ πατρός.
choices.english: Doublet collapsed: first form kept (Colossians 1:13–14); second form's added material under 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: Added material kept: 'but they achieved nothing', 'now ... through the Lord's economy', 'whom he loved' (angels loved as ministers, Christ as Son), 'we are under the heir, not under the household slaves', 'nor is the adversary a son of sin', servants loved vs the Son loved as son, 'so that he might make us worthy of his kingdom', and 'exactly like the one who begot him ... the image of the Father'.

choices.term: Ἵνα σοι δείξῃ ὅτι καὶ πρὸ πάντων ἐστίν … (runs into u01-rem-mid)
choices.english: The second catena form adds: To show you that he is also before all things, he has said that he was also …
choices.why: Unmarked repetition of the 1:15–17 note (it repeats 'if he was not before all things...', 'in him ... hope in Christ, not angels', 'in him = through him'); treated as the second form. Only its new material is printed; it continues into u01-rem-mid.

choices.term: Τί δὲ ἦν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ; τὸ ἐπιγνῶναι ὑμᾶς
choices.english: That you should recognize and know
choices.why: ὑμᾶς is the subject of the infinitive; the old English 'To know you' reversed it.

choices.term: ἀλλ' οὐκ μετέστησεν ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς … ἀλλὰ νῦν
choices.english: Yet that is not how God brought us into his kingdom. It is now, through our Lord …
choices.why: The contrast οὐκ … ἀλλὰ νῦν: the angels' service did not bring us in; the Son did.
Biblical phrases 'sons of disobedience' and 'son of Gehenna'; 'son of perdition' left uncited because the Bible gives it to Judas and the man of lawlessness, not to the devil.

Old English printed '(Col 1:7)' etc. at paragraph ends and gave no label to the second forms; SOURCE_ISSUES item 4 (section tagged 1:7-14 but opening on 1:6 and ending on 1:16-17) is answered by labelling each note by the edition's own label.
